_comment: A/B for #122 (FluidAudio 0.15.4 -> 0.15.5). The same tree was built against each pin in turn and run on osr-harvard-1 (33.6 s, English, multi-chunk) — the corpus whose seams can reach 0.15.5's changed merge code, unlike the jfk/Chinese pairs the first write-up used. An earlier version of this file stored only two error rates, which cannot establish its own headline: two equal WERs do not imply equal transcripts (0.0375 = 3/80, and more than one transcript yields three edits). It also asserted that upstream 0ac0e414's fallbacks were exercised, which measurement refutes. Everything below is a hash a reader can recompute or a count a reader can reproduce.

metric._note: Numerator and denominator are recorded so the value can be re-derived rather than trusted. The three edits are `it's -> it is` (one substitution plus one insertion) and `parked -> park` (one substitution), identical on both arms.

method.command: <realpath of built bestasr> transcribe <audio> --backend fluid-parakeet --model 0.6b-v3 --language en --hallucination-filter off --format srt --output <out>
method.why_transcribe_not_benchmark: `benchmark` writes to ~/.bestasr/store and has no --store-dir, so it cannot be run without touching durable user data — that is what polluted the store during an earlier round and required a row to be deleted afterwards. `transcribe` reads the store for routing and writes nothing.
method.why_explicit_path: `bestasr` is not resolvable on PATH on this machine, so an earlier `bestasr benchmark …` method string described a command that could not run. Invoking by realpath also removes any question of a stale binary elsewhere on PATH.
method.why_srt_and_filter_off: --hallucination-filter off removes post-processing. SRT as well as txt because a moved seam shows up in the timecodes before it shows up in the words.
method.determinism_control: Each pin was run twice; same-pin runs are byte-identical. Without this, cross-pin identity would be uninterpretable — a decoder that drifted run to run would make both sameness and difference meaningless.
method.which_code_ran: `nm` on the built executable counts the ChunkProcessor.caseVariantCanonicalIds symbol: 0 under 0.15.4, 4 under 0.15.5. The executable's own hash is deliberately NOT recorded as identifying evidence — the same pin built twice yields different executable hashes (measured), so it identifies a build, not a dependency. The reproducible pair is the resolved revision plus the nm count.

path_coverage._note: Measured by adding stderr probes to ChunkProcessor at all five changed sites and rebuilding. The probe build's transcript is byte-identical to the clean 0.15.5 build's, so the instrumentation does not perturb the result. This is the half that two earlier write-ups inferred backwards from the output and got wrong in opposite directions — first claiming the fallbacks were exercised, then claiming none of the five was reached.
path_coverage.counterfactual: Each merge was computed twice inside one binary — once with caseVariantIds, once with nil, which degrades tokenIdsMatch to exactly 0.15.4's behaviour. Token ids and timestamps are identical both times. That is why a predicate that was entered and answered differently still produces an identical transcript.

what_it_shows: On this corpus the transcripts are byte-identical across the pin change. That is NOT because the changed code did not run: the case-folded overlap matcher was entered twice and matched a token pair 0.15.4 rejects (ids 375 ` r` and 518 ` R`, canonical 375), and collapseSeamWordDuplicates was called. Neither changed the merge output. Upstream 0ac0e414's three word-boundary fallbacks were never entered. Evidence about the merge path on one English corpus; it does not generalise to corpora whose seams differ in shape.
store_note: An earlier 0.15.4 run wrote a measurements.jsonl row stamped app_version 0.16.0 — the version shipping with 0.15.5 — because the schema has no FluidAudio field, so the row could not say what condition produced it. That row was removed rather than left to be ranked against honest ones; a backup was kept at ~/.bestasr/store/measurements.jsonl.bak-idd122-20260803161704, which is machine-local and therefore not auditable from this repo. The measurements recorded here wrote nothing to the store.
